name: Integrative Biology PhD
summary: PhD-only program that studies whole organisms, from genomes to ecosystems. Students are admitted directly into a faculty member's lab, with no rotations, so applicants are strongly encouraged to contact faculty before applying.

deadlines.label: Application deadline
deadlines.note: The Graduate Division lists November 19, 2026 for the fall term and says applications are due by 8:59 PM PST on the deadline date. The program's own pages give no date; they point to the Graduate Division's list and say letters of recommendation are due the same day.

timeline.interviews: The program's FAQ says there is usually an interview weekend in late January. Selected candidates are invited, and not being invited doesn't mean you aren't being considered.
timeline.decisions: The FAQ says most admission decisions are made by late February or early March, and all offers by mid-April.

english.toefl: 5, with Speaking and Writing 4.5 (tests from 21 Jan 2026); 90 (tests from 1 Jun 2025 to 20 Jan 2026)
english.note: The program lists proof of English proficiency for applicants who don't speak English as a native language; the Graduate Division's rules, shown here, decide who is exempt. IELTS tests from 21 January 2026 also need Speaking and Writing 6.5. Tests taken before 1 June 2025 are not accepted, and neither is Duolingo. Not needed with a degree from a country where English is the main language, a degree taught in English at a regionally accredited US institution, or at least a year of full-time study at such an institution with grades of B or better.

applicationFee.note: $135 for US citizens and permanent residents and $155 for everyone else, plus a 4.22% payment processing fee. Waivers are for US citizens and permanent residents with financial need or from eligible programs.

documents: Letters of recommendation (due by the application deadline)
Proof of English proficiency, if English isn't your first language
Names of IB faculty you would like to work with
requirements.note: The pages don't say how many letters are needed. Contacting potential faculty mentors before you apply is strongly encouraged; the FAQ says their input has significant influence on the review, and not all faculty recruit students every year. Applicants are expected to have the equivalent of a major in a biological science. The FAQ says the GRE is optional, with no minimum score.

funding.note: For students entering in Fall 2026 or later, the department guarantees income for 5 years as long as they meet basic program requirements. The page says this results in at least $37,000 a year plus tuition, fees and health insurance, without naming an academic year for the amount; the guarantee covers in-state tuition and fees. International students are charged non-resident tuition: the FAQ says the program covers it for the first two semesters, then the student makes a funding plan with their faculty mentor, and after advancing to candidacy (in IB, typically after the second year) it can be reduced 100% for up to three years (6 semesters).

international.note: The FAQ says the department is committed to financially supporting all admitted students, including international students.
